lessons_control.note: pre_lessons is each hunter's own sum before it read researcher_us/LESSONS.md. edge_resolve.py ranks it against the same realised move as the key, which is the only thing that can tell the guidance file apart from a habit.

language_control.note: RETIRED 2026-09-22: the European and Canadian hunters now run one bilingual pass and emit no freeze, so this is 0/0 on every run sealed after that date. On earlier runs pre_local is each hunter's own sum after the ENGLISH pass and before the local pass; eu_resolve.py ranks it against the same realised move as the key, per market, and does not pool the UK (where the second pass varied source locality) with Germany and France (where it varied language).

note: Ranked on impact_sum: the hunters' signed per-finding sizes, added up, in points of spot. No call and no threshold -- cut wherever you like afterwards, which is what keeps the ranking question answerable at every k. `conviction` (abs of the key) is where the direction skill lives: over all events the sign is a coin flip, above the median conviction it is 74%. conviction_floor is a floor on emphasis in the note, never a filter on this file. Everything under `diagnostics` was measured as neutral or subtractive and decides nothing -- see researcher_us/EDGE_ANALYSIS.md.

findings.finding: The Q3 seasonal decline the consensus bakes in looks too shallow. Consensus at $181.8M implies -4.3% q/q from Q2's record $189.9M. In Q3 2025 revenue fell -8.6% q/q ($157.4M to $143.8M), and in Q3 2024 it fell about -4.8%. On the Aug 4 call management warned that August vacations would slow centres and that Q3 'may not match Q2's strength'. Repeating 2025's seasonal step gives about $173.6M, a ~4.5% miss. Partial offsets: July 2026 was the highest aviation month in company history (CEO, same call), and the logistics account won from a competitor in Q2 carries into Q3. Net expectation: about a 1% revenue shortfall against the bar.

findings.finding: The company itself scheduled an initial 2027 outlook for the combined Grindr + Freddie (PurposeMed) for this Q3 call, so this print carries a first guide for a new year. Freddie's 2026 revenue is expected above $80M with adj. EBITDA above $10M (about 12.5% margin), against Grindr's FY26 guide of about $540M revenue and about $232M adj. EBITDA at roughly 43%. So the combined 2027 headline revenue should land well above the $592M-$617M aggregator 2027 figures, which most likely exclude Freddie. The combined margin will be diluted below the 39-42% long-term target the company reaffirmed. The core-growth guide is the unknown.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 raised the FY guide by $5M on a 4.3% revenue beat and the stock fell 3.3% (baseline). In Q3 2025 the revenue guide was reaffirmed, EBITDA guidance was raised, and the stock rose 11.0%. In Q1 2026 the guide was raised to $535M and the stock rose 9.3% (baseline). Guidance direction has decided the sign.

findings.finding: Q3 revenue consensus is $136.4M-$136.6M, below Q2 2026's reported $138.1M. That is a sequential decline and only +17.8% year on year against Q3 2025's $115.8M. Q2 showed average paying users of 1.4M (+16% YoY) and ARPPU of $26.51 (+12%), and management wrote it is 'performing ahead of what we expected coming into the year'. The last three revenue prints beat: Q2 2026 by 4.3% ($138.1M vs $132.4M), Q3 2025 by 2.2% ($115.8M vs $113.3M). A Q3 at merely flat sequential revenue ($138M) would beat by about 1.2%. A Q3 2025-style sequential gain would beat by 3-5%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue beats have bought mixed reactions. Q3 2025's 2.2% beat bought +11.0%; Q2 2026's 4.3% beat was sold (-3.3% in the baseline, -6.7% after hours per one recap). This name does not reliably pay for a beat.

findings.finding: Grindr agreed on 2026-09-02 to settle the UK privacy group action for GBP 26M (about $35M): GBP 13M due by 2026-12-31 and GBP 13M by 2027-03-31. The Q2 10-Q showed only $2.6M of accrued legal contingencies at June 30, so most of the charge should hit Q3 GAAP results, about $0.15-0.20 a share before any tax effect, against a $0.16 EPS consensus. Grindr adds back litigation costs in adj. EBITDA, so the guided EBITDA line is unaffected.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 GAAP EPS was reported as a miss ($0.10 vs $0.15-0.16 per aggregators) alongside a revenue beat, and the stock fell 3.3%. That GAAP-line reaction cannot be separated from the guide.

EBITDA guide, and buybacks are already 'more opportunistic'. The money buys a business with revenue above $80M that adds EBITDA dollars, so the sign is near zero.

findings.finding: Beta Bionics, a direct US pump competitor, reported on 2026-10-27. It quantified up to $8.5M of Q4 2026 revenue it may lose as prospective pump users wait for its tubeless Mint (cleared 2026-09-14, full launch Q1 2027). Its pharmacy-benefit channel sales rose 118% y/y while DME rose only 4%. For Tandem the deferral is the risk: its own Mobi tubeless is promised for a 'scaled launch in H2 2026'. If buyers wait for it, the same deferral hits Tandem's implied Q4 US sales of $210-225M (flat to +7% y/y), which the FY guide needs. The pharmacy surge supports Tandem's pharmacy-led US ramp, so I net the two at a small negative.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: TNDM has moved on the guide and the pharmacy narrative more than on the quarter. findings.finding: Management said on the Q2 call (2026-08-06) that the Mobi tubeless 510(k) was submitted in Q2 and that a scaled launch would follow clearance in H2 2026, with 2027 the first full year. openFDA's 510(k) records list Tandem's latest decision as K260429 (Control-IQ+, 2026-04-24) and show no tubeless clearance. With under two months of 2026 left, the call is at risk of pushing the scaled launch into 2027, or of having to explain the timing. The other possibility is that the clearance is announced with the print, which would be a positive surprise.
